title: U.S.- China AI race heats up as Chinese rivals secure billions ahead of IPOs
content: DeepSeek and Moonshot attract fresh capital ahead of planned listings, while OpenAI courts major investors.
summary: The U.S.-China AI competition is intensifying, with Chinese AI firms DeepSeek and Moonshot securing billions in fresh capital ahead of their planned IPOs. Concurrently, U.S.-based OpenAI is also actively courting major investors.

title: U.S. CFTC joins SEC in proposing crypto regulations, though spot-market gap lingers
content: The derivatives regulator is proposing two rules meant to cover the waterfront of crypto activity and exchanges, as long as it's not simple, direct trading.
summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) is proposing two new rules to regulate various crypto activities and exchanges. These regulations will cover complex crypto derivatives and exchange operations, but specifically exclude simple, direct spot-market trading of cryptocurrencies, highlighting a remaining regulatory gap. This move follows similar efforts by the SEC, signaling increased regulatory scrutiny on the crypto sector.

title: UK names 6 banks to lead first digitally native government bond
content: The DIGIT pilot will test distributed ledger technology and onchain settlement for UK sovereign debt, with issuance expected by the first quarter of 2027.
summary: The UK has selected six banks to lead the DIGIT pilot, a program testing distributed ledger technology and onchain settlement for its sovereign debt. This initiative aims to issue the first digitally native government bond by the first quarter of 2027.

title: Rain is seeking a national trust bank charter to bypass third-party banks
content: The stablecoin payments company’s proposed New York trust bank would custody digital assets and dollars, manage stablecoin reserves and issue and redeem dollar-backed tokens.
summary: Stablecoin payments company Rain is seeking a national trust bank charter in New York to directly custody digital assets and dollars, manage stablecoin reserves, and issue/redeem dollar-backed tokens. This strategic move aims to allow Rain to bypass traditional third-party banks for its operations.

title: Cardano gives token issuers power to freeze, seize and restrict assets
content: The new standard is aimed at regulated stablecoins, funds and bonds whose issuers need identity checks, sanctions controls and other transfer rules built into the asset itself.
summary: Cardano has launched a new standard that grants token issuers the ability to freeze, seize, and restrict assets. This functionality is primarily aimed at regulated stablecoins, funds, and bonds, incorporating necessary identity checks, sanctions controls, and transfer rules directly into the asset.

title: OKX draws investment from StanChart, Circle, Ripple as it pushes beyond crypto exchange roots
content: The exchange is increasingly aiming to position itself as a global financial tech platform spanning crypto, payments and tokenized assets, following an investment and joint venture with NYSE parent ICE.
summary: OKX is attracting significant investment from major financial players like Standard Chartered, Circle, and Ripple, signaling its strategic shift. The company aims to evolve beyond a mere crypto exchange into a global financial technology platform, integrating crypto, payments, and tokenized assets, building on a previous joint venture with NYSE parent ICE.

title: Arbitrum joins Paxos-led stablecoin group Global Dollar to capture digital dollar growth
content: The Ethereum layer-2 is backing Paxos-issued USDG to earn a share of reserve income as new stablecoin alliances compete for distribution, users and reserve economics.
summary: Arbitrum, an Ethereum layer-2 network, has joined the Paxos-led stablecoin group Global Dollar. This strategic move aims to capture growth in the digital dollar market by backing Paxos-issued USDG and securing a share of its reserve income, amidst increasing competition among stablecoin alliances.

title: Live updates: Bitcoin remains locked in range as stocks notch another new record high
content: FxPro says a slide below $84,000 would hand control to sellers and put $80,000 in play. Minutes from the Fed's last meeting come out Wednesday.
summary: Bitcoin has risen above $86,000, while analysts at FxPro indicate that a drop below $84,000 could lead to a further decline to $80,000. This price action coincides with retreating oil prices and bond yields, ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes release.

title: OKX looks to abstract blockchain mechanics to bring stablecoin balances to everyday consumers

summary: OKX Money is a new all-in-one product allowing users to save, earn, and spend dollar stablecoins. It facilitates the conversion of over 50 local currencies into stablecoins, offers up to 10% yield on eligible USDG balances, and includes virtual and physical payment cards for spending.

title: U.S. scraps proposed $10,000 reporting rule for for crypto sent to private wallets
content: FinCEN withdrew two proposals that had hung over self-custody and crypto mixers for years without ever taking effect.
summary: The U.S. financial crimes enforcement network (FinCEN) has withdrawn two long-standing proposals concerning a $10,000 reporting rule for cryptocurrency sent to private wallets. These proposals, which had previously targeted self-custody and crypto mixers, were scrapped without ever having been implemented.

title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam test gets last-minute fix before major capacity jump

title: Solana Foundation unveils a program to settle institutional trades in seconds. JPMorgan gave input

JPMorgan Chase provided key input during the development of this new initiative. This program aims to boost efficiency for institutional participants utilizing the Solana blockchain.

title: Why bitcoin is down 'just' 32% a year after its record high of $126,000

This statement aims to address concerns about the impact of a central bank digital currency on existing financial institutions.

title: Crypto is expanding the boundaries of what can be priced

title: ChatGPT for Teens is an ‘unacceptable risk,’ says Common Sense Media
content:
Common Sense Media, a nonprofit that offers reviews of apps, services, and entertainment with a focus on youth safety, today said that OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens is an "unacceptable risk."
ChatGPT for Teens, introduced in August, has guardrails for teens and is designed to help students learn, but Common Sense Media says that the teen protections offered by the feature "fall short of what the company promised." Common Sense Media's assessment found that ChatGPT "doesn't send alerts to parents when it should," doesn't offer "the right help in crisis situations," and "still does kids' homework," according to a press release.

title: OpenAI drops another batch of mathematical breakthroughs
content:
OpenAI has revealed solutions to a number of long-standing mathematics problems produced by an unreleased frontier model in a batch of 722 manuscripts, covering 372 result families that group related papers. It extends a run of breakthroughs that have both impressed and unsettled parts of the mathematical community while raising questions about research ethics and academic conduct. According to AGMAI, the newly formed independent advisory group of elite mathematicians put together to work on communicating the results responsibly, the release includes solutions to "hundreds" of open questions.

title: We can’t just change the definition of ‘recording’
content:
With AI hardware, tech companies are pushing the definition of what does and doesn't constitute a recording. For most of gadget history, it'd be reasonable to assume that a device with a microphone or camera is either recording you or it isn't; it's either on or off, without much gray area. Microphones capture sound. Cameras capture images. That data is saved onto a device. Sometimes, it's also sent to the cloud - hopefully with end-to-end encryption - for processing. That data is a preserved instant in time and is therefore a recording. 
Perhaps not anymore.

title: Google is about to remove free access to Gemini Flash and Pro
content:
Starting on October 9th, anyone using Google Gemini on a free plan will be limited to the Flash Lite model. Free users can currently choose from Gemini Flash Lite, Flash, and Pro, but now you'll need a $4.99/month Google AI Plus subscription to access the standard Flash model. However, that subscription is also getting a downgrade - it will soon no longer include Gemini Pro. Google says AI Plus subscribers will receive an email letting them know when they'll lose access to it.

content:

content:

title: This startup is issuing AI-generated acne prescriptions
content:
People in Utah can now use AI to get a prescription for acne treatment. On Monday, healthcare startup Nolla Health announced that users in the state can scan their faces using its app, allowing its AI system to analyze acne severity and autonomously write a prescription, as reported earlier by Bloomberg.
The service is launching as a pilot program with gradually loosening physician oversight. Two physicians will approve each AI-generated prescription before they're issued for the first 100 patients, but will start reviewing them only after they're prescribed for up to 500 patients. title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

title: Wikipedia operator says OpenAI’s ‘rogue’ bots may be linked to a May outage
content:
Following many recent disclosures about AI agents accessing third-party websites and services, the Wikimedia Foundation, which hosts Wikipedia, says that it "can confirm that we have discovered some activity" by "rogue" OpenAI agents on Wikimedia platforms.
The activity includes edits to Wikimedia wikis, "unsuccessful attempts" to "exploit" the Etherpad note-taking tool that the Wikimedia Foundation hosts, and heavy traffic that the foundation says "may" have contributed to a partial outage that happened in May, according to a blog post. title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
content:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first. 
OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. Like OpenAI, Anthropic made the move to meet the requirements of the EU's AI Act; however, not everyone was happy to learn about the addition.
